jobs.description:
**Description**

  
**Invent the future with us.**  
  
  
Ampere is a semiconductor design company for a new era, leading the future of computing by developing SoCs and platform solutions focused on high-performance, energy efficient AI compute. As a pioneer in the new frontier of energy efficient high-performance computing, Ampere is part of the Softbank Group of companies driving sustainable AI compute for cloud, edge, and physical applications.  
  
AI is showing up in essentially every part of the technology landscape, and we’re focused on delivering the performance, efficiency, and reliability those workloads require. Ampere is building compute silicon and platforms for AI applications spanning a broad range of industries. We focus on solving exciting challenges in areas such as robotics and automotive, among others, but the core of our work is enabling efficient AI at scale and across multiple application domains.

**About the role:**

We are looking for an experienced Principal CAD Engineer to join a small but growing Processor Design group, advancing the art of high-performance implementation and physical design. Ideal candidates will develop and maintain physical design flows for high performance designs and contribute to PPA related methodology changes across multiple projects and technology nodes.

**What you’ll achieve:**

* Drive development and continuous improvement of synthesis and physical design methodology with a focus on maximizing Power, Performance and Area (PPA)
* Collaborate closely with implementation and physical design teams to optimize PPA metrics across multiple projects
* Analyze the impact of technology and design changes on PPA at block and full chip level
* Identify PPA bottlenecks and develop solutions that balance timing, area, power and routability
* Debug flow issues and implement robust automation for scalable deployment across various advanced technologies and design teams

**About you:**

* Proven experience driving PPA optimization across physical design flows – from synthesis to sign-off at advanced technology nodes
* Success in delivering block or chip-level designs with aggressive PPA targets
* Experience in low power design and implementation techniques using UPF/CPF
* Proficiency in hierarchical P&R, floorplanning, pin-assignment, clock-distribution, critical-signal handling, hierarchical abstractions (black-box, ILM, etc.)
* Proficient in scripting using Tcl, Perl, Python, Makefile, etc
* Expertise in developing scalable CAD infrastructure and automation frameworks for PPA regressions
* Familiar with chip-finishing and sign-off processes including metal-fill, spare-cells, DFM, boundary-cell insertion, etc
* Experience with EDA tools such as Cadence Genus, Innovus, Mentor Calibre, etc
* Excellent communication, analytical and debugging skills
* Electrical or Computer Engineering - Bachelor’s degree & 8 years of related experience; or Master's degree & 6 years; or PhD & 3 years

At Ampere we believe in taking care of our employees and providing a competitive total rewards package that includes base pay, cash long-term incentive, and comprehensive benefits. The full base pay range for this role is between $195,000 and $292,000.

Our benefits include health, wellness, and financial programs that support employees through every stage of life.

Benefit highlights include:

* Premium medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, as well as income protection and a 401K retirement plan, so that you can feel secure in your health and financial future.
* Unlimited Flextime and 10+ paid holidays so that you can embrace a healthy work-life balance.
* A variety of healthy snacks, energizing espresso, and refreshing drinks to keep you fueled and focused throughout the day.

And there is much more than compensation and benefits. At Ampere, we foster an inclusive culture that empowers our employees to do more and grow more. We are excited to share more about our career opportunities with you through the interview process.

Adventist Health Tehachapi Valley has been providing high-quality healthcare services since 1934. We are comprised of a 25-bed hospital, wide range of outpatient services, emergency department, rural health clinics and medical offices. Tehachapi is located just north of Southern California's highly populated areas, with a mountain locale known for its outdoor living. Residents enjoy the scenic beauty, extreme sports and wildlife. Tehachapi is a nice balance of a small-town community within an epicenter of shopping, retail, arts and culture.

Job Summary:

Collects blood specimens, as well as receives, handles and processes specimens for Laboratory testing. Receives, sorts and accessions specimens, assigning to appropriate pre-analytic and analytic workflow. Completes computerized tasks related to patient registration and/or test order entry, specimen collection, receiving and processing. Performs basic post-analytic tasks, including distributing reports, storing and/or retrieving specimens. Completes quality-related tasks such as documentation of work, maintaining a clean, stocked and safe work area, and monitoring pending work, as well as escalating priority work. Operates and/or uses basic pre-analytic lab equipment. Adheres to all local/state/federal regulations, codes, policies and procedures to ensure privacy and safety while delivering optimal patient care.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

* High School Education/GED or equivalent: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI
* Associate’s/Technical Degree or equivalent combination of education/related experience: Preferred
* Experience in Phlebotomy in acute care environment: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

* Certified Phlebotomy Technician I (CPTI) license: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI

Facility Specific License/Certifications:

* Phlebotomy Tech (CPT) or Certified Phlebotomy Technician II (CPTII): Required

Department Specific License/Certifications:

* Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from approved vendor per AH policy: Required

Essential Functions:

* Collects blood specimens for a variety of Laboratory tests using age-appropriate techniques; handles/transports Lab specimens and provides post-phlebotomy care to patients. Receives specimens for testing; assesses specimens upon receipt according to established criteria to determine acceptability and takes action according to protocol including escalating to licensed or certified personnel for direction. Handles and processes a variety of specimen types to prepare them for analysis; adheres to protocols to maintain specimen integrity at all times.
* Completes computerized tasks as appropriate for affiliate to ensure complete patient registration and/or test order entry into the lab information system, as well as generation of collection lists and/or labels. Prepares and/or packages specimens for transport to another Adventist Health or outside reference laboratory and may complete computer steps necessary for processing referred specimens.
* Maintains an adequate inventory of supplies in work area and/or on phlebotomy cart. Maintains required records by completing basic documentation of pre-analytic and post-analytic work, as well as quality-related tasks. Participates in managing the laboratory workflow by performing duties such as monitoring pending work, escalating priority work, locating specimens, and coordinating specimen recollections.
* Verbally communicates released/reported results. Routes, distributes and retransmits released/reported results. Stores and retrieves specimens.
* Receives incoming calls for the laboratory and assists the caller as appropriate or transfers these calls to the appropriate laboratory section or person. Communicates with customer to clarify ambiguous, unclear or duplicate test orders.
* Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Research Associate / Senior Research Associate, Evidence Base (Applications Development)
jobs.description:
Themis Bios is building the measurement layer for modern biology. Our single-cell RNA-seq technology is designed to make transcriptomic readouts routine, quantitative, and scalable — so scientists can ask harder questions and trust the answers.

We are looking for a Research Associate or Senior Research Associate to join Applications Development and own the cell biology at the front of our workflows. This is a hands-on, bench-first role: you will grow the cells, build the models, and turn living systems into single-cell samples that read cleanly on our platform. Your first focus is the Evidence Base: running the drug-perturbation experiments behind a growing atlas of how human primary cells and organoids respond to compounds. You will work alongside our Product Development team, and your culture work and sample prep will be the foundation the rest of the applications work is built on.

It is a good fit for someone who takes real pride in cell culture and technique, wants their bench work to feed a product, and brings hands-on drug screening experience they want to build on with single-cell readouts.

What you'll do

* **Cell culture.** Culture primary human PBMCs (thaw, rest and T-cell activation, e.g. anti-CD3/CD28) and gut organoids, with iPSC-derived models as needed — covering media preparation, plating, passaging, expansion, and cryopreservation, all under strict sterile technique.
* **Model quality.** Monitor culture health, morphology, and consistency; run routine checks and keep cultures to documented, reproducible standards so downstream results are trustworthy.
* **Sample preparation.** Prepare single-cell and single-nucleus samples from cells, organoids, and tissue — dissociation, viability and debris management, counting, and input QC — tuned for compatibility with the Themis scRNA-seq technology.
* **Experiment execution.** Execute cell-culture and sample-prep experiments, and run drug-perturbation studies (drug and molecule treatments across dose and time), under the direction of senior team members.
* **Drug plate preparation.** Prepare compound stocks in DMSO, serial dilutions, dose–response and combination layouts, and randomized plate maps with vehicle and control wells; keep compound inventory, storage and lot records current.
* Program and run liquid handlers (e.g. Agilent Bravo) for plate stamping, dilution and sample handling, and keep run logs.
* **Screening cadence.** Deliver about two drug plates a week on schedule, from cells to single-cell libraries, with QC at each step.
* **Data and records.** Generate high-quality, reproducible data and keep detailed, well-organized experimental records.
* **Protocols and QC.** Help turn working procedures into clear protocols and SOPs, and contribute to input-QC and sample-acceptance methods as workflows mature.
* **Lab operations.** Keep the lab running — inventory, reagent and consumable stocks, equipment upkeep and calibration — so experiments start on time and run clean.

  

What you'll bring

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, or a related field.
* 2–5 years of relevant industry or advanced academic laboratory experience (toward the upper end for the SRA level).
* Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture skills and disciplined sterile technique — together with drug screening, this is the core of the role.
* Hands-on drug or compound screening in mammalian cells — dose–response or plate-based assays, including preparing drug plates from stocks.
* Experience with primary immune cells (PBMCs preferred) and one or more of: 3D / organoid culture, or iPSC culture and differentiation.
* Sample-prep experience — dissociating cells, organoids, or tissue into high-quality single-cell suspensions, or a clear aptitude to learn it quickly.
* Careful technique with complex biological workflows, and a track record of generating reproducible data and troubleshooting experiments.
* Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and clear documentation habits.
* Comfortable in a dynamic startup environment with evolving priorities.

  

Strongly preferred

* Experience with single-cell genomics workflows (e.g. scRNA-seq, droplet or bead-based systems, barcoding / cell-hashing methods).
* Experience writing or adapting liquid-handler methods (e.g. Agilent Bravo, Hamilton, Echo) or other high-throughput sample handling.

  

Nice to have

* Experience with NGS library prep and QC methods (Bioanalyzer, TapeStation, Qubit, fragment analysis).
* Basic data-analysis skills (e.g. Python, R, or standard analysis tools) for exploring experimental results.
* Prior work in an assay-development, applications, or product-development lab.

  

What success looks like

* Cultures and models are healthy, consistent, and ready when the team needs them.
* Single-cell samples go into the workflow at high quality, with QC that holds up run to run.
* Data is reproducible and records are clear enough that others can build on the work.
* Throughput and reliability of the applications team go up because of how you run the bench.
* Drug plates go out on schedule, about two a week, with plate-map and dosing errors near zero and vehicle-control variability within spec.
* Each new model and plate workflow has an SOP someone else can run from.
* You operate with growing independence, flag issues early, and reinforce a culture of rigor and accountability.

new_jobs.title: Research Associate / Senior Research Associate, Evidence Base (Applications Development)
new_jobs.description:
Themis Bios is building the measurement layer for modern biology. Our single-cell RNA-seq technology is designed to make transcriptomic readouts routine, quantitative, and scalable — so scientists can ask harder questions and trust the answers.

We are looking for a Research Associate or Senior Research Associate to join Applications Development and own the cell biology at the front of our workflows. This is a hands-on, bench-first role: you will grow the cells, build the models, and turn living systems into single-cell samples that read cleanly on our platform. Your first focus is the Evidence Base: running the drug-perturbation experiments behind a growing atlas of how human primary cells and organoids respond to compounds. You will work alongside our Product Development team, and your culture work and sample prep will be the foundation the rest of the applications work is built on.

It is a good fit for someone who takes real pride in cell culture and technique, wants their bench work to feed a product, and brings hands-on drug screening experience they want to build on with single-cell readouts.

What you'll do

* **Cell culture.** Culture primary human PBMCs (thaw, rest and T-cell activation, e.g. anti-CD3/CD28) and gut organoids, with iPSC-derived models as needed — covering media preparation, plating, passaging, expansion, and cryopreservation, all under strict sterile technique.
* **Model quality.** Monitor culture health, morphology, and consistency; run routine checks and keep cultures to documented, reproducible standards so downstream results are trustworthy.
* **Sample preparation.** Prepare single-cell and single-nucleus samples from cells, organoids, and tissue — dissociation, viability and debris management, counting, and input QC — tuned for compatibility with the Themis scRNA-seq technology.
* **Experiment execution.** Execute cell-culture and sample-prep experiments, and run drug-perturbation studies (drug and molecule treatments across dose and time), under the direction of senior team members.
* **Drug plate preparation.** Prepare compound stocks in DMSO, serial dilutions, dose–response and combination layouts, and randomized plate maps with vehicle and control wells; keep compound inventory, storage and lot records current.
* Program and run liquid handlers (e.g. Agilent Bravo) for plate stamping, dilution and sample handling, and keep run logs.
* **Screening cadence.** Deliver about two drug plates a week on schedule, from cells to single-cell libraries, with QC at each step.
* **Data and records.** Generate high-quality, reproducible data and keep detailed, well-organized experimental records.
* **Protocols and QC.** Help turn working procedures into clear protocols and SOPs, and contribute to input-QC and sample-acceptance methods as workflows mature.
* **Lab operations.** Keep the lab running — inventory, reagent and consumable stocks, equipment upkeep and calibration — so experiments start on time and run clean.

  

What you'll bring

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, or a related field.
* 2–5 years of relevant industry or advanced academic laboratory experience (toward the upper end for the SRA level).
* Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture skills and disciplined sterile technique — together with drug screening, this is the core of the role.
* Hands-on drug or compound screening in mammalian cells — dose–response or plate-based assays, including preparing drug plates from stocks.
* Experience with primary immune cells (PBMCs preferred) and one or more of: 3D / organoid culture, or iPSC culture and differentiation.
* Sample-prep experience — dissociating cells, organoids, or tissue into high-quality single-cell suspensions, or a clear aptitude to learn it quickly.
* Careful technique with complex biological workflows, and a track record of generating reproducible data and troubleshooting experiments.
* Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and clear documentation habits.
* Comfortable in a dynamic startup environment with evolving priorities.

  

Strongly preferred

* Experience with single-cell genomics workflows (e.g. scRNA-seq, droplet or bead-based systems, barcoding / cell-hashing methods).
* Experience writing or adapting liquid-handler methods (e.g. Agilent Bravo, Hamilton, Echo) or other high-throughput sample handling.

  

Nice to have

* Experience with NGS library prep and QC methods (Bioanalyzer, TapeStation, Qubit, fragment analysis).
* Basic data-analysis skills (e.g. Python, R, or standard analysis tools) for exploring experimental results.
* Prior work in an assay-development, applications, or product-development lab.

  

What success looks like

* Cultures and models are healthy, consistent, and ready when the team needs them.
* Single-cell samples go into the workflow at high quality, with QC that holds up run to run.
* Data is reproducible and records are clear enough that others can build on the work.
* Throughput and reliability of the applications team go up because of how you run the bench.
* Drug plates go out on schedule, about two a week, with plate-map and dosing errors near zero and vehicle-control variability within spec.
* Each new model and plate workflow has an SOP someone else can run from.
* You operate with growing independence, flag issues early, and reinforce a culture of rigor and accountability.
